reason: This passage from Exodus 14 demonstrates Moses exemplifying responsible leadership for the people's welfare. When the Israelites become afraid and complain to Moses (v. 11-12), he responds by taking direct responsibility for their spiritual welfare, reassuring them: 'Do not fear; stand firm and see the salvation of the Lord which He will perform for you today' (v. 13-14). Moses then acts as the instrumental leader by following God's command to lift his staff and part the sea, directly ensuring the people's physical safety and deliverance (v. 16-22). Throughout the narrative, Moses functions as the intermediary leader accountable for guiding the people through crisis—addressing their fears, providing leadership direction, and taking action that results in their welfare. The passage shows leadership predicated on taking responsibility for people's security and welfare, which aligns with the statement's core concept.
